chunks: From him, from Sa'id ibn Janah, from a number of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Kaaba, in the era of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), was nine cubits, and it had two doors. Then Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr rebuilt it and raised it to eighteen cubits. Then al-Hajjaj demolished it and rebuilt it to twenty-seven cubits.

key_terms.أذرع/ذراع: Cubit — a unit of measurement approximately 46–56 cm, measured from elbow to fingertip
key_terms.الحجاج: Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi — infamous Umayyad governor of Iraq who demolished Ibn al-Zubayr's reconstruction
key_terms.الكعبة: The Kaaba — the sacred cubic structure at the center of al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca
key_terms.عبد الله بن الزبير: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr — companion of the Prophet and briefly recognized caliph who renovated the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What were the dimensions of the Kaaba during the time of Ibrahim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates the architectural history of the Kaaba from the time of Prophet Ibrahim through later Islamic history. The original structure was a modest nine cubits high with two doors; it was significantly expanded by Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, then further altered by al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi, the Umayyad governor notorious for his heavy-handed rule. This hadith preserves knowledge of the sacred structure's dimensions as understood within the Shia tradition and reflects ongoing interest among the Imams in the authentic history of the Kaaba.
